ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The directions and magnitudes of three known forces are as follows: $\mathrm{F}_{1}{=}20\mathrm{N}$, directed at a 37-degree angle to the horizontal, upward to the right; $\mathrm{F}_{2}\mathrm{=}6\mathrm{N}$, vertically downward; $\mathrm{F}_{3}\mathrm{=}10\mathrm{N}$, horizontally to the left. It is known that $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$ and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. Find the magnitude of the resultant force $F_{all}$ of the three forces.
2. Find the direction of the resultant force $F_{all}$ of three forces.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$6\sqrt{2}N$
The direction is at a 45^{\circ} angle to the positive x-axis, pointing to the upper right.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the coordinate axes indicate that the positive x-axis points to the right and the positive y-axis points upward. Force F1 is directed obliquely upward to the right from the object, lies in the first quadrant, and makes an angle of 37° with the positive x-axis; force F2 is vertically downward; force F3 is horizontally to the left. Then reason: Take rightward as the positive x direction and upward as the positive y direction. It is known that F1=20 N, and sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, so the components of F1 are F1x=20cos37°=20×0.8=16 N, F1y=20sin37°=20×0.6=12 N. From the directions in the figure, F2=(0,-6) N, F3=(-10,0) N. The resultant force components are Fall=(16-10,12-6)=(6,6) N. The magnitude of the resultant force is |Fall|=sqrt(6^2+6^2)=sqrt72=6sqrt2 N. Since the x and y components are both positive, the resultant force is in the first quadrant; the direction angle theta=arctan(6/6)=45°, that is, it makes 45° relative to the positive x-axis and points upward to the right.
